The Record

A few things I built, and a few doors I opened

2022UPS Foundation

The relationships outlasted the role

At the UPS Foundation, I helped oversee a $50M+ philanthropic portfolio across 1,000+ partner organizations. I left that role in mid-2022 — but the trust I'd built with people there didn't expire when my badge did.

2023The Carter Center

Using influence after I no longer had a title to use it from

Months after leaving UPS, I was working on grant proposals for the Carter Center's global health and governance programs. One of their initiatives needed funding I knew UPS could plausibly support. I wasn't a UPS employee anymore and it wasn't part of my Carter Center job description — but I made the introduction anyway. That relationship led to $20,000 in funding for a program that mattered.

It's a small story, but it's the one I point to when people ask what "relationship-building" actually looks like in practice: it's rarely transactional, and it doesn't stop when the org chart says it should.

2023–2026Bobby Dodd Institute

Building a legislative presence from almost nothing

When I stepped into this role, Bobby Dodd Institute — an organization with over 30 years of history serving people with disabilities in Georgia — had fewer than 10 active relationships with state legislators. Advocacy happened, but it wasn't structured, and it wasn't sustained.

Over three consecutive Georgia Legislative Sessions, I built that number to over 100 within two years and past 150 relationships by year three — legislators and staff who knew BDI's name, understood its work, and were willing to act on its priorities. I organized town halls that put elected officials directly in front of the people our programs served, secured buy-in for legislative site visits, and represented the organization at the Georgia Capitol and on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC.

That sustained presence led to a Georgia House of Representatives resolution formally recognizing BDI's impact — a level of institutional recognition the organization hadn't achieved in three decades.

2024–2026Bobby Dodd Institute

A federal seat at the table

I also represented BDI and SourceAmerica — an AbilityOne-authorized nonprofit connecting federal agencies with disability employment providers — before federal agencies and congressional staff in Washington, DC, engaging directly on procurement and policy priorities affecting people with disabilities. I coordinated a U.S. Department of State– and IREX-funded exchange initiative that brought 20+ delegates from 10+ African nations to the U.S., partnering directly with State Department and IREX officials to manage travel, housing, and university placements across a genuinely complex, multi-country logistics environment.

2025Bobby Dodd Institute

Building the pipeline that didn't exist

BDI had never had a structured internship program in its 30+ year history. I designed and launched one from scratch — defining the role, the onboarding, and the mentorship structure — and brought on five interns through it. It's a smaller number than the legislative work, but it's the one that will outlast my time there: a pipeline that keeps bringing new people into the organization's mission.
